title: What is known about 1RB0RE_1LC0RA_1LD0LC_0LE0LB_1RA1RF_0LC---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0RE_1LC0RA_1LD0LC_0LE0LB_1RA1RF_0LC---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. Lean proves fourteen shift rules (C going left turns every c = 100 into d = 101, D leaves it; A and E cross pairs going right). The visited tape grows on the left like the square root of time; the halting question sits at the irregular wall between the bouncer and the frozen tail, whose rule was not derived.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: Shift rules over c = 100 and d = 101
claims.text: Going left, C turns (100)n into (101)n and D leaves it; A and E cross pairs of words going right; B crosses the tail word 110100 both ways.

claims.title: Where it can halt
claims.text: Only F reading 1 halts; F is entered only from E reading 1 (1RF), so the machine halts exactly on E> 1 1. Read off the table.

claims.title: The tape over time
claims.text: With c = 100, d = 101: at step 108 0 c3815 1 [C0] d83 00 c11 1 d 00 ...; at 4·108 0 c4022 1 [B1] d 00 1 d3805 00 1 d5 ...; at 109 0 c3955 1 0 [E0] 0 1 d8435 00 c 1 d2 ...; at 2·109 0 c11883 d [A0] 1 d5646 00 1 d 00 ...; each followed by an irregular stretch and a long tail (1 d 00)n = (110100)n.

claims.title: A bouncer whose sweeps trade c for d
claims.text: The head sweeps the left part; going left in state C it turns c into d, going right it works in pairs; the boundary between the c-part and the d-part moves back and forth (the bands of the space-time diagram). Observed only.

claims.title: No closed tape language with small windows
claims.text: bbtools.ctl K = 3..6 leaves halting configurations; n-gram CPS 3 to 7 fails; no invariant mod 2..12.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 38,451 cells have been visited and 21,467 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.462). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.032).

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The machine stops only on E> 1 1; the clean c/d sweeps and the tail never make it, so the question is about the irregular wall between them, whose evolution was not derived.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this Turing machine has run for 10<sup>9</sup> steps without stopping. This page runs the real machine in your browser, shows the shape of its run, and lists what is known, each result marked by what it rests on.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 38,451 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The growth shape of the two sides of the tape (see below).

sections.heading: Words 100 and 101, a wall, and a frozen tail
html:
Write c = 100 and d = 101. At step 2·109 the tape is

0 c^11883 d [A0] 1 d^5646 00 1 d 00 c^3 1 d 00 c 1 d^2 00 ... (1 d 00)^n

On the left a long run of c then d (the part that grows like a square root), in the middle a short irregular wall, on the right a long tail of 110100 words that hardly changes (the part that grows like a logarithm).

sections.heading: Sweeps that trade c for d
html: Lean proves fourteen shift rules. Going left in state C the head turns every 100 into 101; in state D it leaves them alone. Going right, A and E cross the words in pairs. So each sweep moves the boundary between the c-run and the d-run, which is what the bands in the space-time diagram show: at step 108 there are 3,815 c and 83 d next to each other, at 4·108 4,022 and 3,805, at 109 3,955 and 8,435, at 2·109 11,883 and 5,646.

sections.heading: Only on E> 1 1
html: Only F reading 1 stops the machine, and F is reached only from E reading 1 and stepping right, so it stops exactly when E stands on 1 1. That never happens inside the c/d runs or the tail; the wall between them is where it could, and its rule was not found.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.462). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.032).
After 109 steps the tape spans 38,451 cells (28,255 left of the start, 242 right), with a density of 1s of 0.558.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

summary: A bouncer over 3-cell words c = 100 and d = 101: the sweeps on the growing left part trade c for d and back, next to a small irregular wall and a frozen tail of 110100 words on the right.
